summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease Hb-SS and a history of osteosarcoma was admitted for persistent abdominal pain and constipation, initially thought to be related to proctitis. Imaging revealed a rectal mass with extensive lymphadenopathy, prompting a flexible sigmoidoscopy that identified a 1 cm abnormal mucosal area; biopsy confirmed poorly differentiated rectal adenocarcinoma. Staging with PET and MRI showed metastatic disease (T4B, N2, M1). She developed intermittent rectal bleeding requiring two units of packed red blood cells. Cancer-related pain was managed by initiating long-acting morphine, while her home Dilaudid was continued for breakthrough pain. Hydroxyurea was held due to thrombocytopenia. A port was placed and a CT-guided pelvic lymph node biopsy performed for tissue confirmation; results were pending at discharge. She was discharged home with a plan to follow up in the multidisciplinary rectal cancer clinic for chemotherapy initiation.
